title: Globular cluster NGC 6752
caption: Part of the globular cluster NGC 6752, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble view shows part of NGC 6752, a globular cluster, one of the dense, ancient balls of stars that orbit our galaxy. At the top left, a collection of faint stars marks something nobody expected to find there, a galaxy far beyond the cluster.

Astronomers pointed Hubble at NGC 6752 to study its white dwarfs. A white dwarf is the small, dense remnant left behind when a Sun-like star uses up its fuel, and because white dwarfs cool at a predictable rate, they can be used as clocks to measure a cluster's age.

While analysing the data, the team spotted the previously unknown galaxy lying behind the cluster. It was nicknamed Bedin 1. The galaxy was an unexpected bonus, since a study aimed at the cluster's own faint stars also turned up a far more distant neighbour hiding in the background.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys imaged the field through a visible and a near-infrared filter. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Faint white dwarfs and the background galaxy are far too dim for the eye, but Hubble's long exposures and near-infrared light, which the eye cannot see, bring them out.

behind.people: See full credit: ESA/Hubble, NASA, Bedin et al.
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image was taken with Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and credited to ESA/Hubble, NASA and Bedin and colleagues.
alt: Stars of a globular cluster, with a faint patch of stars marking a background galaxy at the top left.
